issues.legal_issue: An acquisition award outside the specified transitional period may qualify for increased solatium when a literal application of the transition provision would produce an anomalous exclusion inconsistent with its purpose.
material_facts: The acquisition began before the amendment introducing increased solatium.
The Collector made the initial award before the transitional period began.
The reference court made its award after the amendment came into force, but outside the transitional period specified in the transition provision.

A literal reading of the transition provision would have denied increased solatium despite the amendment’s purpose of extending the higher rate to awards made during the transition and awards otherwise covered by the amended provision.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was entitled to increased solatium, and the High Court’s award of solatium at the higher rate was left undisturbed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 23(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, as amended, provides increased solatium, while Section 30(2) sets out its transitional application. Although Union of India v. Raghubir Singh, following Kamalajammaniavaru v. Special Land Acquisition Officer, held that the transitional provision ordinarily applies where the Collector’s or court’s award was made within the specified period, the Court construed the provision to avoid an anomalous result contrary to its purpose and potentially vulnerable under Article 14. It applied the interpretive approach in Mahadeolal Kanodia v. The Administrator General of West Bengal; Bhag Singh and State of Punjab v. Mohinder Singh had been overruled by Raghubir Singh.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and acquisition_started_before_transition and collector_award_preceded_transition and reference_award_followed_amendment and literal_cutoff_excludes_comparable_later_award and exclusion_conflicts_with_transition_purpose

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The case is an appeal concerning compensation awarded for an acquired parcel of land.
predicates.acquisition_started_before_transition: The acquisition proceedings began before the statutory transition period began.
predicates.collector_award_preceded_transition: The Collector made the initial award before the statutory transition period began.
predicates.reference_award_followed_amendment: A court deciding the compensation reference made its award after the amendment introducing increased solatium came into force.
predicates.literal_cutoff_excludes_comparable_later: A literal application of the transition cutoff would exclude an award made after the specified transition period.
predicates.exclusion_conflicts_with_transition_purp: The exclusion would treat a later award less favourably than awards the transition provision was intended to benefit, producing an anomalous result.

issues.definition: When an acquisition compensation appeal concerns an acquisition begun before the transition, an earlier Collector’s award, and a later reference award, increased solatium applies if the literal cutoff would anomalously exclude the later award contrary to the transition provision’s purpose.

issues.legal_issue: An additional compensation amount is unavailable when the acquisition began before the transition date and the Collector had already made an award before that date.
material_facts: The acquisition proceedings began before the transition date for the additional amount.
The Collector made the award before that date, so no proceeding remained pending before the Collector on that date.
The claimant sought the additional amount in the later compensation proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was not entitled to the additional amount, and the High Court’s award of it was deleted.
issues.legal_principle: Section 23(1A) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, provides an additional amount, but Section 30(1)(a) applies it to proceedings pending before the Collector on the transition date in which no award had yet been made, and Section 30(1)(b) applies it to proceedings commenced after that date. The amount therefore does not apply where the acquisition began earlier and the Collector had already made the award before the transition date. The Court rejected the contrary approach of the Karnataka and Bombay High Courts, which had relied on Bhag Singh, because Bhag Singh was overruled by Union of India v. Raghubir Singh.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding: The proceeding concerns compensation for land acquired by the state.
predicates.acquisition_started_before_transition: The acquisition proceedings began before the statutory transition date for the additional amount.
predicates.collector_award_preceded_transition: The Collector made the initial award before that transition date, leaving no acquisition proceeding pending before the Collector on that date.

issues.definition: When an acquisition compensation proceeding concerns an acquisition begun before the transition date and the Collector had already made an award by that date, the additional compensation amount is unavailable.
